text:
nightly-evals: :rotating_light: regression detected in nightly eval (job id 20250415-03). rdx-13b with int8-profile-v3 shows ~6% drop on math suite and clear quality failures on summarization prompts. full diffs in dashboard: https://dash.internal.redwood/evals/20250415-03

Aisha: saw the alert, digging in — dropping INT8 profile into staging prod yesterday (quant-profile-v3). Noticed calibration step used 'chatty_dialogues.json' set, might be mismatch for math prompts.

Jonathan: which commit rolled the profile?

Aisha: rolled with commit 7f3a1b2 (deploy/quant-profiles) at 02:12 UTC. The profile changed symmetric->asymmetric per-channel and enabled per-layer zero-point clipping.

Maya: :eyes: can you paste a minimal repro eval command? I'll kick a quick run on a GPU box.

Aisha: run this locally to reproduce:
```bash
./tools/run_eval \
  --model rdx-13b \
  --quant-profile int8-profile-v3 \
  --eval-sets nightly/math,nightly/summarize_short \
  --seed 42 \
  --output /tmp/quant_reg_out.json
```

Rachel: I ran that on a p3.2xlarge clone, confirmed math accuracy down from 78.9 -> 72.4 (FP16 baseline). Summarization ROUGE-1 dropped ~0.08.

Jonathan: sample bad generation from summarization set (prompt id 1287):
"""
Prompt: Summarize the article about satellite imagery use in disaster response.
FP16: "Rescue teams used satellite images to map flooded areas, enabling faster allocation of resources and reduced response times. The study highlights..."
INT8-v3: "Satellites are used to fly faster and make water, team go to there. The map green then rescue go." 
"""

Maya: wow — very degraded fluency and hallucination spike. Does the loss happen during calibration (per-layer scales) or during runtime kernel selection?

Aisha: initial hypothesis: calibration set mismatch caused extreme scaling for certain layers (attention output) so quant zero-points saturate and KV cache dynamics break. Also saw increased L2-norm of activations in layer 21 during calibration logs.

eval-bot: attached calibration summary: top offending layers by scale variance: [layer_21, layer_34]. max_scale_ratio=28.4x.

Jonathan: can we quickly re-run calibration with the smaller, more diverse calib set (calib/representative-1k.json) and compare? If numbers recover, it's clearly calibration-data drift.

Aisha: starting re-cal with representative-1k now on ded-gpu-03. command:
```bash
python tools/calibrate_quant.py \
  --model checkpoints/rdx-13b/7f3a1b2 \
  --calib-set data/calib/representative-1k.json \
  --out profiles/int8-profile-v3-recal.json
```

Rachel: small experiment idea: try symmetric per-channel quant (disable asymmetric/zero-point clipping) and see if fluency improves. Also test FP8-proxy run (fp8-emulation) to check if lower precision path is generally ok.

Maya: putting both jobs in queue: recalibrate + symmetric run. If recalibrated profile recovers >3% of lost accuracy I'll mark v3 as 'unsafe' and revert to v2 in hosted routing.

Aisha: temporal note — we pushed v3 to dedicated yesterday afternoon under canary flag; routing for hosted remained v2. Good we caught it in nightly.

(20m later) Maya: recal finished. Quick numbers: recal-profile recovered math from 72.4 -> 76.8 (still -2.1 vs FP16), summarization ROUGE-1 up to 0.03 above int8-v3 but still below FP16.

Aisha: partial recovery suggests calibration set was a big factor but not full story. Any kernel differences between deploys? eng-runtime recently landed an optimized GEMM kernel that switches block size based on seq_len; maybe interaction with asymmetric quantization.

Jonathan: pinging eng-runtime channel — @eng-runtime any recent kernel changes that could affect quantized runtime behavior?

Rachel: also tried symmetric per-channel: that gave slightly better fluency (less hallucination) but worse math (precision decreased). Tradeoff between numeric fidelity and language fluency.

Aisha: proposed next steps:
- roll back int8-profile-v3 in Dedicated routing (canary off) until full triage done :white_check_mark:
- run targeted layer-wise ablation: re-run inference forcing full-precision on layer_21 and layer_34 to measure sensitivity
- get eng-runtime to reproduce with new kernel flags disabled/enabled to isolate runtime interaction
- run a quick FP8-emulation test to see if fp8 path would be viable at all
- open an incident ticket if we see customer impact in logs

Jonathan: I'll open PR to pin int8-profile to v2 in the model catalog and add a safety check to nightly-evals to alert on max_scale_ratio > 10x.

Maya: added the reproducer job to the 'quant-triage' queue and attached logs here: https://ci.internal.redwood/quant-triage/8743/logs

Aisha: thanks all. If someone from eng-runtime can join a quick 15-min sync (in 30m) that'd be great. I'll also gather a small set (~10) of worst-offending prompts to include in regression alerts. :+1:

eng-runtime (external): acknowledged — will join.

Rachel: final note — marking this thread resolved for now after rollback and queued triage. Will update once we have layer-ablation numbers. :white_check_mark:
